title: Portrait and Visitor
premise: Theo Crane returns to her grandmother's house to bury her twin sister Wren, only to find the funeral arrangements already made—for Theo. The house's photographs keep gaining an extra chair, and the town's founding families have been feeding something in the orchard for two hundred years, a debt renewed each harvest moon by one of the Crane line. Theo, who documented everything to feel real, discovers her sister's hidden journals revealing that Wren took her place in the ritual once before—and intends to again. In the orchard under the rising moon, Theo must choose between finishing the founders' ritual as written or breaking it entirely, and she learns that belonging was never something the house gave; it was something it collected.
about_author: E. M. Reyes is the pen name of a former archivist who spent six years cataloguing estate photographs in rural New England, where she learned that every family keeps one box no one is allowed to open. She writes horror about houses that remember more kindly than the people who lived in them.

chapters.title: The Wrong Sibling
chapters.summary: Theo arrives at grandma's house with Wren's ashes and finds a funeral notice bearing her own name, dated tomorrow. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: disorientation sharpening into dread as the house's hospitality feels rehearsed, like it expected someone else—or exactly her.

chapters.title: Inventory of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Theo photographs every room to steady herself, a coping habit since childhood, but the developed images show an extra wooden chair in each frame—empty, facing the camera. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: the comfort of documentation curdling into evidence that something wants to be seen.

chapters.title: What the Founders Planted
chapters.summary: At the wake, elderly neighbors speak in ritual phrases about 'the orchard's share' and flinch when Theo mentions twins. Aunt Marguerite warns her to leave before the moon fills. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: isolation—the town's warmth is loyalty to something older than any guest.

chapters.title: Wren's Handwriting
chapters.summary: Searching for burial clothes, Theo finds Wren's hidden journals: their grandmother's death was scheduled, Wren volunteered as the harvest's tithe years ago, and the entries grow increasingly written in a hand that isn't quite hers. POV: Theo with journal excerpts. Emotional beat: grief complicated by betrayal—her sister kept the truth to protect her.

chapters.title: The Chair at Dinner
chapters.summary: Theo sets the table for one; by candlelight there are settings for two, and the extra chair is warm. She interviews Marguerite, learning the founders bound a presence in the orchard with an inheritance of names—and twins confuse the ledger. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: terror braided with a shameful flicker of being wanted.

chapters.title: Ledger of Names
chapters.summary: In the church basement, Theo reads the founders' ledger: every Crane generation has paid, and Wren's name appears twice—once crossed out, once fresh ink, dated the coming moon. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: rising urgency as she realizes the house isn't haunting her; it's invoicing her.

chapters.title: Everything I Kept
chapters.summary: Theo confronts Wren's ghost—or memory—in the orchard at dusk; Wren explains she traded herself for Theo once already and means to finish it, because loyalty meant choosing which sister got to live visible. POV: alternating Theo and Wren's final journal entry. Emotional beat: heartbreak—the horror is love, misapplied.

chapters.title: Harvest Moon Rising
chapters.summary: Marguerite and the neighbors arrive not to save Theo but to ensure the debt is paid, sealing the doors. The chair now sits at the head of the table, and the photographs show Theo seated in it. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: claustrophobic climax pressure—no exit except through the ritual.

chapters.title: The Ritual, Rewritten
chapters.summary: In the orchard, Theo begins the founders' rite but alters it: she offers the ledger itself, the record of debts, burning page by page while naming every taken ancestor aloud. The presence in the trees hesitates, hungry for a name it can finally keep. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: defiant clarity—truth spoken aloud against inherited silence.

chapters.title: Portrait, Unframed
chapters.summary: Dawn. The extra chair is gone from every photograph; Wren's second name has faded to blank paper. Theo buries both sisters' ashes together and leaves the door unlocked behind her. Final image: a new photo on the mantel—Theo, smiling, alone, uncollected. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution—belonging chosen, not owed.
